metadata.title: Rachaad White catches touchdown in Week 3 win over Seahawks
metadata.description: Rachaad White rushed eight times for 35 yards while also hauling in his only target for six yards and one touchdown in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: White has heated up out of the backfield of late, finishing with 40 or more offensive yards in each of the first two contests. The running back offers more value in PPR formats as part of a backfield shared with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, with a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts up next.

metadata.title: Rachaad White - Reaches end zone in victory
metadata.description: White rushed eight times for 35 yards and caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown during Sunday's 33-31 win over Seattle.
metadata.analysis: White was far more productive over his eight carries (4.4 YPC) than starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was on his 19 rushes for 36 yards (1.9 YPC). White's most notable moment of the game came as a pass-catcher though, securing a six-yard touchdown on a pass from Marcus Mariota in the first quarter. Through three games so far in the regular season, White has compiled 100 rushing yards on 22 carries while catching all nine of his targets for 51 yards and a score.

metadata.title: Rachaad White - Makes return to Sunday's contest
metadata.description: White (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's game against the Seahawks in the third quarter, JP Finlay of NBC Sports Washington reports.
metadata.analysis: White earned three touches and recorded a receiving touchdown in the first half before getting banged up shortly before the end of the second quarter. After receiving treatment during halftime, White looks like he'll be able to fill a change-of-pace role out of the Washington backfield for the rest of the contest.

metadata.title: Rachaad White (shoulder) questionable to return
metadata.description: Commanders RB Rachaad White is questionable to return Sunday due to a shoulder injury.
metadata.analysis: White had four rushing yards on two carries and one receptions for six yards prior to the injury. Jacory Croskey-Merritt will continue to see the bulk of the carries with White sidelined.

metadata.title: Rachaad White - Iffy to return Sunday
metadata.description: White is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Seahawks due to a shoulder injury.
metadata.analysis: With White leaving Sunday's contest, Washington could lean more on its other backfield options if he's unable to return. He had been working in a complementary role and seeing pass-game involvement for the Commanders.

metadata.title: Rachaad White Returns After Shoulder Injury
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White (shoulder) returned to Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks after leaving shortly before halftime. White was initially listed as questionable to return, but JP Finlay reported that he was back on the field in the second half. He had two carries for four yards and caught a six-yard touchdown before leaving. White has already added two more carries since returning, bringing him to four rushes for 12 yards on the afternoon. His return is encouraging after the earlier scare, though it does not necessarily mean the shoulder issue is completely behind him.

metadata.title: Rachaad White Questionable to Return
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks with an apparent shoulder injury, David Harrison of Locked On Commanders reported via the X platform. White had two carries for four yards before exiting Sunday's game.

metadata.title: Rachaad White Projects As Flex Option in Week 3
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White had a strong performance in Week 2's loss to the Cowboys, handling seven carries for 43 yards and adding six catches (six targets) for 40 yards as a receiver. White earned more work after a quiet Week 1 and ended up evenly splitting touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, with 13 each. White may see more opportunities moving forward as Croskey-Merritt has struggled some early on. White has not yet found the end zone as a Commander, and that will be a tough ask again in Week 3 against the Seattle Seahawks, who have not allowed a rushing touchdown yet this season. White has a safer floor in PPR formats, though the ceiling of Washington's offense is lower with Marcus Mariota in place of Jayden Daniels (elbow). White projects as a decent flex option and ranks as RotoBaller's RB44 for Week 3.

metadata.title: Rachaad White - Highly efficient in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: White rushed seven times for 43 yards and brought in all six targets for 40 yards in the Commanders' 37-20 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: The Commanders fell into catch-up mode throughout the second half, a situation tailor-made for White's pass-catching acumen. The veteran offseason addition saw a hefty workload as a result, recording four more catches on four additional targets than he'd seen in Week 1. White is likely to continue in a complementary role behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt for the time being, but the former figures to continue seeing plenty of run anytime the Commanders are trailing.

metadata.title: Rachaad White hauls in six passes in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Rachaad White rushed for 43 yards on seven carries in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys. He caught 6-of-6 targets for 40 yards.
metadata.analysis: White saw six targets to Jacory Croskey-Merritt's one target, but both contributed the same amount of yards on the ground. With Jayden Daniels (elbow) out for the foreseeable future, the running game should get more of a focus heading into a Week 3 matchup with Seattle.

metadata.title: Rachaad White Profiles as RB3 Option in Week 2 at Cowboys
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White was quiet in the Week 1 loss to the Eagles, handling seven carries for 22 yards and adding two receptions (two targets) for five yards. White wasn't able to create much with his opportunities against a tough defense and was firmly behind second-year back Jacory Croskey-Merritt as the team's primary runner. The former Buccaneer played 40.3% of the offense's snaps compared to 49.3% for Croskey-Merritt, and it's worth noting that Croskey-Merritt didn't return after his fumble on Washington's final drive. Washington will likely continue to operate with a split backfield in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys, who got lit up by the Giants in their season opener. Dallas allowed 4.5 yards per carry and four catches to running backs, potentially setting White up for a productive day. White projects as a low-end flex for Week 2, ranking as RotoBaller's RB42 in PPR leagues.

metadata.title: Rachaad White's Inefficiency and Low Volume a Major Concern
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White appears to be solidified as the team's clear No. 2 option out of the backfield. There was some speculation that he was signed to compete for Jacory Croskey-Merritt's lead-back role, but there was a clear gap between the two in Week 1, as White rushed for just 22 yards on seven carries. His low volume and lack of efficiency make him an unappealing fantasy option going forward. His role as a handcuff makes him a worthwhile stash in most leagues, but he does not belong in starting lineups as long as Croskey-Merritt is healthy. RotoBaller's fantasy football experts agree, dropping him to RB41 in their latest rankings for half-PPR leagues ahead of Week 2.

metadata.title: Rachaad White sees nine touches in Week 1
metadata.description: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 22 yards while also catching both of his targets for five yards in the Commanders' 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
metadata.analysis: White made the most of modest touches in the season-opening contest, finishing second to Jacory Croskey-Merritt in touches in the loss. The running back offers more value in PPR formats as the No. 2 backfield option for the Commanders, with a Week 2 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

metadata.title: Rachaad White - Quiet in Commanders debut
metadata.description: White rushed seven times for 22 yards and caught two of three targets for five yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: White had a long run of nine yards but was held to 13 yards across his other six carries. He did see a substantial amount of action, logging 27 offensive snaps to Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 33, with Kaytron Allen mixing in for six snaps. White was the only one of the trio to gain positive yards through the air, and he's likely to feature as the Commanders' top pass-catching back in 2026 while mostly deferring to Croskey-Merritt on the ground.

metadata.title: Rachaad White in Flex Territory for Week 1
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White has been a reliable fantasy producer over the last few seasons, with some upside mixed in at times. The 27-year-old finished as high as the RB10 in PPR/G in 2023, recording the fourth most receptions among running backs in the league that season with 64. White's inefficiencies as a runner have limited his overall upside to this point in his career, though he's still one of the most effective pass-catching backs in the league. Washington's offense missed the receiving ability of RB Austin Ekeler after he got injured early last season, which is the role that White is now aiming to fill. Jayden Daniels doesn't throw to his running backs at an extreme rate. Still, Ekeler played 17 total games with the Commanders (including playoffs) and averaged 3.7 targets and 3.1 catches per game, which are similar to White's career numbers. It remains to be seen how White works into the offense alongside Jacory Croskey-Merritt, but White is expected to play an important role early. White has a challenging matchup in Week 1 against the Eagles, ranking as RotoBaller's RB35 in PPR leagues.

metadata.title: Rachaad White (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
metadata.description: Rachaad White (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
metadata.analysis: The veteran running back is fully over his hamstring injury at this point and is set to be a full go for Washington's season opener on Sunday. He will be primed for more work if Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is limited or sidelined for the team's matchup against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Rachaad White - Clear of injury report
metadata.description: White (hamstring) wasn't listed on the Commanders' initial Week 1 injury report Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: White had been tending to a hamstring issue since mid-August, but his ability to avoid the practice report entirely Wednesday indicates he's put the injury behind him. Meanwhile, Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited to kick off Week 1 prep, leaving one big question mark in Washington's backfield ahead of Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

metadata.title: Rachaad White (hamstring) set to practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Rachaad White (hamstring) is set to take part in Washington's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: White's status for Week 1 is still unclear right now thanks to a hamstring injury that he's still dealing with. He is taking part in Wednesday's practice, however, which is a step in the right direction for him. Fantasy managers should pay attention to updates about his health throughout the week, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt will be a significantly better fantasy option if the veteran is sidelined this week.
